facts.text: Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe is based in Southampton County, Virginia.
The Tribe's historical account records an elected Chief and Tribal Governing Council in May 2002.

source.title: Ethno-Historical / Current Snapshot of the Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Nation of Southhampton County, Virginia

facts.evidence: election of a Chief and Tribal Governing Council

facts.text: The Tribe's language page publishes a vocabulary drawn from materials dating to March 4, 1820.
facts.evidence: source materials dating back to March 4th, 1820

facts.text: The Tribe describes Cattashowrock Town's trails as using Iroquoian and English signs to identify local plants and animals.
facts.evidence: Iroquoian language and in English identifying Native Flora and Fauna

nations.name: Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia
nations.lands: southeastern Virginia along the Nottoway River; the Tribe's Community House & Interpretive Center is in Capron

facts.text: The Tribe's history describes the Nottoway as Iroquoian speakers of southeastern Virginia.

source.title: Tribal History - Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

facts.text: According to the Tribe's history, Edy Turner petitioned the Virginia General Assembly on behalf of her people in 1821.

source.title: Tribal History - Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

facts.evidence: In 1821, matriarch Edy Turner petitioned the Virginia General Assembly

facts.text: The Tribe says its Community House & Interpretive Center formally opened in Capron on May 5, 2012.

source.title: Community House & Interpretive Center - Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

facts.evidence: Community House & Interpretive Center in Capron, VA
